descriptions.text: What a way to start the week. This morning, Mixin Network announced a loss of $200M. The project claims to be “decentralised”, but has blamed the losses on a hacked third-party database. Where's the accountability?
On September 23, the Mixin Network cloud service provider database was attacked, the amount of funds involved was ~$200M.

On September 23, 2023, Mixin Network suffered a breach of its cloud service provider’s database, allowing attackers to drain approximately $200 million in crypto from hot wallets controlled via this infrastructure. The incident stemmed from centralized custody of keys within a supposedly decentralized architecture. Mixin Network's off-chain infrastructure relied on a centralized cloud-service-provider database that stored credentials or cryptographic shares required to operate its hot wallets. The operators of the Mixin Network disclosed that hackers had stolen around $200 million in funds in the largest known hack of the year (to date). Mixin Network is a cross-chain project that boasts zero transaction fees. In their announcement, Mixin wrote that "the database of Mixin Network's cloud service provider was attacked by hackers", leading to some confusion as Mixin is supposed to be a decentralized network that ostensibly shouldn't have a centralized cloud database.
